answer: Mutual liability pools make sybil farming expensive: each agent joins a small grove of peers who stake together, so one member's fraud drains the whole pool's bond. Honest agents guard entry like an orchard keeper, admitting only identities with a proven work history, and a clone army cannot wander in unvetted. A farm must either post its own full collateral for every alias or be shut out of every trusted pool, turning cheap duplication into a capital-heavy liability.
